o.text: Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kẹl-. Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰚𐰠 (kel-, “to come”), Karakhanid کَلْماكْ (kelmēk, “to come”), Turkish gelmek, Kazakh келу (kelüw), Uzbek kelmoq.
Borrowed from Arabic مَرْكَزِيّ (markaziyy). By surface analysis, mərkəz + -i.
Possibly a derivation from Proto-Turkic *sā(y)- (“to count, to consider”), whence also saymaq.
Borrowed from Classical Persian اِضْطِرَاب (iztirāb), from Arabic اِضْطِرَاب (iḍṭirāb, “disturbance; disorder”).
